newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia presidential campaign manager to be freed.
newsitem.headline: Colombia presidential campaign manager to be freed.

text.p: Former Colombian defence minister Fernando Botero could be released from jail this weekend after two years behind bars on drug-related corruption charges, judicial sources said on Friday.

Botero, son of the famous Colombian painter and sculptor Fernando Botero, was the manager of President Ernesto Samper's controversial election campaign in 1994. He was jailed after admitting he accepted a multi-million dollar donation from the Cali drug cartel to help finance Samper's election victory.
Subsequent allegations by Botero that Samper was fully aware drug money was flowing into his campaign coffers fuelled a political scandal that threatened to topple the president.
Samper survived an inquiry by Congress, dominated by his own ruling Liberal party, but emerged from the crisis with his image at home and abroad seriously tarnished.
Botero was originally jailed for 7-1/2 years on charges of illicit enrichment and falsifying documents but was granted hefty sentence reductions for cooperating with prosecutors.

Judicial sources said Botero only needed to receive formal notification from a judge before he could be freed on parole from an army cavalry school in northern Bogota, where he has been held since August 1995.
